bugClass.title: Serial CI stages exceed the job time limit
bugClass.cause: A single CI workflow job executes all check stages serially, so cumulative runtime approaches or exceeds its timeout; there is no parallel job split or headroom guard to keep execution within the limit.
bugClass.criteria: Match when a workflow defines one job that sequences multiple check stages and their combined runtime can consume the job timeout, without parallelizing stages or enforcing a runtime/headroom guard. Each condition is sufficient: serial accumulation toward the timeout, or lack of a guard against it. Exclude cases where the limit is exceeded by one independently slow stage rather than cumulative serial work.

candidates.evidence: Lines 92–97 define a whole-check plan containing multiple steps and return those steps for execution, which may enable serial accumulation. The excerpt does not show how runSteps executes them, whether a single CI job invokes the whole plan, or any job timeout, so the triggering workflow and timeout exposure are unestablished.
Lines 102–114 show setup commands run sequentially with per-step timeout fallback to the test timeout. The excerpt does not establish a CI workflow job, cumulative stage runtime, or job timeout.

This test excerpt asserts a 60-minute timeout on a `check-part` matrix job at lines 15–21, but does not show the workflow’s job stages or serial accumulation; the timeout assertion alone cannot establish the candidate cause.
